question: The distance from Chandigarh to Amritsar is covered in 4.5 hours at a speed of 50 km/hr. By how much should the speed (in km/hr) be increased to save 30 minutes of travel time?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time: S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂

⇒ 50 × 4.5 = S₂ × (4.5 − 0.5)

⇒ 225 = S₂ × 4

⇒ S₂ = 56.25 km/hr

Increase in speed = 56.25 − 50 = 6.25 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6.25 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial time (T₁) = 4.5 hours

Initial speed (S₁) = 50 km/hr

Time to be saved = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

New time (T₂) = 4.5 − 0.5 = 4 hours

 
• 
 
 
 Chandigarh
 Amritsar
 Total Distance = 50 × 4.5 = 225 km
 Case 1: S = 50 km/hr, T = 4.5 hrs
 Case 2: New Speed, T = 4.0 hrs
 New Speed = 225 ÷ 4 = 56.25 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 50 × 4.5 = 225 km

⇒ New Speed (S₂) = Total Distance ÷ New Time

⇒ S₂ = 225 ÷ 4 = 56.25 km/hr

⇒ Required increase in speed = S₂ − S₁

⇒ Increase in speed = 56.25 − 50 = 6.25 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6.25 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relationship of Speed and Time

When the distance remains constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). Therefore, S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Average Speed

Average Speed is the ratio of total distance traveled to the total time taken: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. When they move in the same direction, it is |S₁ − S₂|.
